g.text: One wide table, and the three anomalies it creates
Ada's details are stored twice — and will be stored again on every future order.
You must find and update EVERY row,
or the table now disagrees with itself.
A new customer who hasn't ordered
has nowhere to live. No order, no row.
Delete Ada's only order and you
All three are the same problem: one fact — Ada's email — is stored in more than one place.
Normalization is just 'store each fact once, and point at it.'
